bug_semantics: The affected clients place caller-controlled payment, refund, advanced-payment, and disbursement identifiers directly into URL path template literals. Because the identifiers are not passed through encodePathParam/encodeURIComponent, '/', '..', and '?' remain URL syntax; WHATWG URL resolution can change the requested endpoint or add attacker-controlled query parameters while RestClient still sends the merchant's bearer token.
flaw_origin: Commit 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657 is the smallest modern-client BIC: it created src/clients/paymentsRefunds/create/index.ts, get/index.ts, and getList/index.ts and first wrote the unencoded `/v1/payments/${payment_id}/refunds...` RestClient.fetch paths named by the advisory. Later commits extended the same direct-interpolation pattern to payment operations and, in adcaceaa233f5c7cb67d4723d6b7ca0cfdd25e2b, to advancedPayment/disbursementRefund; renames and comment-only changes did not originate the flaw.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names human author and committer Bruna Campos <bruna.camposf@mercadolivre.com>; its complete message is `payment refund client` and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: GitHub advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8vxq-h2gr-x277 and VulnCheck's CVE-2026-76842 record identify the vulnerable payment, paymentRefund, advancedPayment, and disbursementRefund clients, the unencoded template-literal mechanism, affected mercadopago <=3.4.0, and PR #451 as the partial hardening that left these clients unchanged.

`git show 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657 -- src/clients/paymentsRefunds/{create,get,getList}/index.ts` shows three new files whose RestClient.fetch paths directly interpolate payment_id (and refund_id) without encoding. `git log -S'/v1/payments/${' -- src/clients` places this commit first among the modern src/clients implementations; later additions include payment capture 6008b53014be88d6757e89ec42688ce7d8906fe0, cancel 0fdb24947c5f0e211d49e6d169f53b461c1dc2c3, get 203000cd6d49d416ff8a50ca4cae290da4b92b13, refund total 3c58ca7b51d8917681b56d5ae17265d21c047d4c, and advancedPayment/disbursementRefund adcaceaa233f5c7cb67d4723d6b7ca0cfdd25e2b.

`git rev-parse 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657^` returns 6ad06e6670735c3881c8925ba25000593eddbb83. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 6ad06e6670735c3881c8925ba25000593eddbb83 -- src/clients/paymentsRefunds/create/index.ts src/clients/paymentsRefunds/get/index.ts src/clients/paymentsRefunds/getList/index.ts` returns no paths, and the BIC patch shows the predecessor src/clients/refunds operation files were empty; the vulnerable path-building lines are therefore absent from the immediate parent tree.

`git tag --contains 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657 --sort=version:refname` starts at 2.0.0 and includes 3.4.0. Tag 2.0.0 is cb7eb3603b4acf13aa8dc65ab1741df1542f2d77; tag 3.4.0 resolves to 9a197d3c3f1950930ba6908ed6c2caa821ef78b9, matching the advisory's cited vulnerable snapshot.

PR #451 merged as 068e5d8e4ba0518872533c58cca8cd9a2a8a6d55 from direct commit 66daf6b95fc7768741ee8460d74dbda95e8cd586. Its changed-path list adds src/utils/path.ts and encodes other client families but contains none of payment, paymentRefund, advancedPayment, or disbursementRefund, so neither SHA is a fix for this case.

At validated clone head c8da864cd370d179ad10e182e4793510d6d03bfe (tag 3.6.0), the named client files still contain unencoded `/v1/payments/${...}` and `/v1/advanced_payments/${...}` template literals. Thus releases 3.5.0, 3.5.1, and 3.6.0 made after the <=3.4.0 disclosure boundary remain vulnerable; no public fix commit or patched release boundary exists in this history.

`git cat-file -p 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657` shows one parent, author and committer Bruna Campos <bruna.camposf@mercadolivre.com>, and only the message `payment refund client`; this BIC commit object has no AI attribution marker.
reasoning: The first surviving implementation of the advisory's modern RestClient.fetch flaw is the small, ordinary commit 7d83325f4760a079a0d3f3f69001c07a8d380657, not a later rename, comment pass, endpoint expansion, or PR #451's incomplete hardening. It made the new client architecture vulnerable by writing three attacker-influenced URL path segments without percent-encoding; subsequent payment and advanced-payment commits copied/extended the same mechanism. Direct inspection of parent 6ad06e6670735c3881c8925ba25000593eddbb83 proves those files and lines absent, and tag containment places the BIC before the first 2.0.0 release and the cited vulnerable 3.4.0 boundary. PR #451 supplied the intended encoder to other clients but omitted every family in this advisory, and current tag 3.6.0 still has the vulnerable paths, so fix_sha/direct_fix_sha are justified nulls rather than the partial-hardening SHAs. Finally, only the selected BIC commit object was used for attribution: it has a human author/committer and no AI marker, yielding NOT_AI even though later endpoint additions or refactors are outside the BIC-only decision.
remaining_gap: The vulnerability is still unpatched at validated public-history head c8da864cd370d179ad10e182e4793510d6d03bfe (3.6.0), so no real fix SHA, direct-fix SHA, or patched version boundary can yet be recorded.
